title: Which trials supply individual data, and what selection on it does
question: When the trials that supply individual data are selected on observed trial variables or on their own effect modification, how biased is the interaction evidence, does combining with aggregate trials help, and can a leave-IPD-out diagnostic reveal it?
design: Twelve trials with trial-specific interactions and IPD availability depending on an observed trial variable and on the latent interaction; within-trial and combined estimators; leave-IPD-out influence. 18 cells, 1000 replicates each.
answer: Selection of which trials supply individual data on an observed trial variable caused no bias, but selection on the trials' own effect modification biased the within-trial interaction evidence by up to 0.14 (true 0.3), with coverage down to 0.59. Combining with the across-trial association in all trials halved the bias. A leave-IPD-out influence diagnostic did not respond to the selection, so the problem is invisible without a stated selection model.
findings: Selection on the observed trial variable only: within-trial bias -0.003 to 0.003.
Selection on the latent interaction: within-trial bias 0.027 to 0.142; combined 0.014 to 0.065.
Leave-IPD-out influence 0.026 to 0.046, varying with the IPD share but not with selection strength (correlation with bias -0.85 at half the trials supplying data).
not_answered: Pairwise continuous-outcome meta-analysis rather than component ML-NMR; no selection-model sensitivity analysis; one network size. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Mean treatment-by-covariate interaction and the effect at covariate 1
methods_compared: pooled within-trial interaction from IPD trials
